_: The measured performance bar, read by scripts/gates/perf.py.
The bar itself, the method and the current medians are owned by
docs/architecture/foundation.md section 1 (commitment 2). This file is the
machine-readable copy the gate reads - keep the two in step.
WHY THERE IS A MACHINE CLASS AT ALL:
the scan budget is wall-clock, and roughly a third of it is Tantivy, which
uses min(cores, 8) indexing threads. A 2-core CI runner is plausibly ~3x
slower on that phase through no fault of the change under test. Asserting
the 13 s number on such a runner would produce a gate that fails randomly,
and a gate that fails randomly is a gate people learn to ignore.
So the gate REFUSES TO ASSERT below min_cores rather than scaling the
number by a fudge factor. A skipped measurement is honest; a measurement
adjusted by a guess is not.
BENCHMARKS:
each entry names the crate and example to run, an argv template, and the
regex that pulls a median out of its stdout. Templates substitute {tmpdir},
{size} and {runs}. 'gate_repeats' says who takes the median: false means
the harness runs 'runs' times itself and prints one median (scan_bench),
true means the gate invokes the command 'runs' times and takes the median
of the parsed values (layout_bench, which measures a single run).
Running perf.py with no --benchmark measures EVERY entry here. That is
deliberate: a declared ceiling that nothing runs is not a budget.
reference_machine: 10-core arm64 darwin (the machine the medians were taken on)
